cases.title: Traverse buffered nonunique index pages
cases.failure_hypothesis: Failure to buffer the outer native index cursor could invalidate it when child-group iteration starts; applying a record limit to the outer list would truncate a complete index-key group.
trace: Seed four records spanning blue, green and red with overlapping memberships.
Fully consume limit-one and continuation reads, then dedupe and reverse reads.
Read two bounded reverse primary-key pages within blue.
cases.oracle: First blue page a,b; next green page a,c; first two keys deduped a,b,c. Reverse two keys d,c,c,a; deduped d,c,a. Blue get pages b then a. Full records are literal expectations.
cases.distinctness: T029 characterizes raw native iterator invalidation; D207/D208/K215/K216 cover low-level listing. This case exercises the actual OS module nested index traversal and documented key-count versus record-count semantics, with option permutations combined into one case.

cases.title: Roll back conflicting index subscriptions
cases.failure_hypothesis: A conflict in the second unique subscriber could retain writes made by the first subscriber, damage the old registration, or poison a later successful indexed replacement.
trace: Seed two valid indexed registrations.
Attempt one ordinary conflicting replacement and one conflicting insertion using another existing mail key.
Compare exact entire native keyspace to original literal state.
Perform a valid replacement and compare exact native rows/indexes and reconstructed group records.
cases.oracle: Both legal conflicts identify existing b; a,b and original unique/nonunique keys survive unchanged. Valid a becomes slug gamma/mail c/team blue/revision3; old alpha/a-mail/red keys absent, team counter2 unchanged, blue group has a,b.

cases.title: Transition nullable multikey memberships
cases.failure_hypothesis: Scalar, array and null membership transitions could remove retained intersections, leak last-member group rows, retain nullable unique aliases, or reuse retired group IDs.
trace: Seed two pending draft records, one with no unique alias.
Move a to scalar draft and check shared group retention.
Move a through scalar-to-array-to-null and b to scalar; check reclaimed groups.
Recreate a array and alias memberships; verify the literal complete native keyspace.
cases.oracle: Draft group1 is retained. First pending group0 and final group2 are reclaimed; counter remains3. Recreated a memberships allocate pending3/final4, counter5; b remains draft1 and beta; a regains alpha.
cases.distinctness: Those cases maintain SQL triggers, partial SQL indexes or FTS postings. This case executes the actual OS addIndexSubscriber array/scalar/null delta algorithm and nonunique child reclamation; actual action history schema returns both scalar and array index keys.

cases.title: Rebuild newly declared storage indexes
cases.failure_hypothesis: A late index migration could omit old records, leave stale child rows on repeated rebuild, reset the persistent allocation counter, or make the next indexed edit inconsistent.
trace: Persist two records under an unindexed schema; stop using that schema.
Declare unique slug and nonunique tags and observe empty new indexes before writes.
Invoke both production rebuild methods and version stamp inside one typed transaction.
Rebuild again, checking counter and fresh child IDs.
Perform a post-migration indexed edit and compare literal complete storage.
cases.oracle: First rebuild returns migration-v2 with version2/counter2 and blue a,b/red b. Second rebuild has counter4 and groups blue2/red3, no old children. Edit b yields slug second-v2/tags green4, counter5; a stays blue2 and version2 persists.
cases.distinctness: T208 explicitly rebuilds a synthetic SQL ancestry relation; D211 clears raw storage; T008 nests raw transactions. This is the production module migration API, including its physical child sweep and intentionally retained allocation counter.

cases.title: Delete buffered indexed groups safely
cases.failure_hypothesis: Deleting a nonunique group while index subscribers and application callbacks open native list cursors could invalidate the unbuffered member traversal, skip selected records, or leave secondary postings.
trace: Seed four records, red a,b,c and overlapping shared a,c,d; d is blue.
Subscribe an application remove callback that fully reads the shared index and stores an audit row.
Invoke production tags.delete(red); unsubscribe in finally.
Compare deletion receipts, surviving full record, full audit rows and complete secondary native keyspace.
cases.oracle: Delete receipts3 then0; only d/four/[blue,shared] survives; audits a/one,b/two,c/three. Only slug four and blue2/shared1 child d remain; group counter3 persists.
cases.distinctness: T029 triggers raw iterator invalidation, D210 is raw batch deletion, T027 restores a raw delete and T207 extracts a synthetic partition. This executes production nonunique delete buffering across real index-subscriber native list calls plus an ordinary read-and-audit callback. No callback timing oracle is asserted.
